title: Who's Who: Cecily Morcant
summary: Museum registrar whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Cecily Morcant (born 1834) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a museum registrar whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Morcant led the 1874 custody tests that suggested a retrieval could change in association with its name and documented handling. She introduced duplicate, sealed histories so investigators could compare an object’s treatment with the story told about it.
Whether her results reveal a change in the Referent remains fiercely disputed.

For Alderwick readers, Cecily Morcant stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
